subject: Term handoff & hybrid multi-year structure — Acme Commerce renewal coordination
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme-commerce.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Term structure discussion for upcoming renewal

Hi Sara —

Hope you're well. We're starting prep for the renewal window that kicks on 2027-10-01 for Acme Commerce and wanted to align early on term/structure preferences so we can lock pricing and a rollout plan. High-level options I have in mind that I wanted your input on: 

1) 12-month with opt-in auto-renew (60-day notice) + annual true-up
2) 36-month stepped ramp: year 1 smaller commit + year 2/3 step-up, quarterly true-up year 1, annual thereafter
3) Multi-entity co-term overlay: co-term the four subsidiaries onto a single consolidated commit with per-subsidiary consumption tracking and a blended discount

We can also do a hybrid: firm minimum annual committed capacity with an accelerated quarterly true-up for the first 12 months while we stabilize load. That helps Acme avoid over-committing up front while giving you predictable unit pricing and burst capacity.

Questions for you: which of the above feels closest to Acme's procurement appetite? Any constraints from procurement or treasury around auto-renew or multi-year lock-ins? If helpful I can sketch a phased workload ramp and a recommended pricing ladder.

If you're available I can set a 30-minute call next week with Marissa and Karthik from Renewals to walk through the model. Attaching a quick intake sheet to capture your constraints.

Attachment: Acme_renewal_requirements.xlsx (Excel — requirements and entity list)

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez

- Co-terming the four subsidiaries is preferred operationally — reduces admin overhead.
- Procurement generally wants annual true-ups, but we can agree to quarterly true-ups for the first year if that helps bridge forecasting risk.
- Auto-renew is OK as long as there's a 60–90 day formal notice window and a pricing protection clause for the first 12 months of any renewal.
- Our legal team (cc'd Miguel) will need to see sample terms for tiered discounts and ramp language — specifically definitions for ‘committed capacity’ vs ‘burst capacity’.

Marissa / Karthik / Monica —

Forwarding Sara's intake (attached) and summary above. Key asks from Acme: co-term across 4 entities, quarterly true-up for first year (then annual), opt-in auto-renew with 60–90 day notice, and a strict definition ask from legal on committed vs burst.

Proposed move from sales: quick hybrid that minimizes procurement friction —
- Year 1: 12-month base commit (consolidated across entities) with quarterly true-up and access to burst at a uplifted unit price.
- Years 2–3 (if customer picks 36mo staircase): step-up discounts month 13 onward with an explicit discount ladder tied to committed increase thresholds.
- Auto-renew: opt-in at deal execution; notice window 60 days; price increase cap for first renewal year of 7%.

Draft attached: draft_term_handoff_v1.pdf — contains a sample clause set and a proposed commit ladder. Can you provide pricing ranges (blended discount) and flag any terms that Legal will push back on?

Diego — good framing. A few suggestions from Renewals & Pricing: 

1) Staged co-term overlay
- We can consolidate the four subsidiaries onto a single master commitment with per-entity metering. This reduces paperwork for Acme and allows blended pricing. We'll require a signature from each legal entity on the master schedule (standard practice).

2) Hybrid true-up approach (recommended)
- Q1–Q4 (first 12 months): quarterly true-up applied to consumption over committed baseline. This gives Acme runway to tune usage.
- After month 12: switch to annual true-up unless they elect to keep quarterly at a premium.

3) Auto-renew language (opt-in)
- 60-day notice is acceptable. Add a 7% cap on price increases for the first renewal period to address procurement concerns.

4) Pricing ladder & discounts
- Send to Pricing for exact numbers, but rough guidance: 10% blended discount at base commit, incremental 3–5% bands for each material step-up. We'll model a 24–36 month staircase with milestone-based pricing.

5) Legal redlines to expect
- Definitions around ‘burst’ vs ‘committed’ (we'll include clear KB: burst = short-lived on-demand tokens at Xx cost multiplier).
- Request for SOC 2 evidence and audit log retention — include redacted artifacts link.

Next steps: Pricing will produce a pricing_grid_acme.xlsx by EOD Thursday. Karthik, please coordinate Legal to pre-approve the master schedule template and the opt-in auto-renew clause (cc Miguel on final).

Attachment: pricing_grid_acme.xlsx (Pricing ranges — draft)

Sara / Miguel —

Thanks for the input and for the filled intake. To confirm the path forward that we discussed internally with Renewals:

Agreed structure (proposed):
- Master consolidated commit across Acme's four entities with per-entity metering; each entity signs the master schedule.
- Year 1: 12-month base consolidated commit with quarterly true-up (months 3/6/9/12). Burst capacity available at a defined uplift.
- Optional 24–36 month staircase: customer can elect at any time to convert to a multi-year stepped ramp with milestone discounts applied retroactively from conversion date.
- Auto-renew: opt-in at signature, 60-day notice window, price increase cap 7% for first renewal year.

Requested action items:
1) Miguel/legal: please review the attached final_terms_v2.pdf and confirm whether the master schedule signature approach is workable and whether Acme needs entity-level amendments.
2) Sara/contracts: can you confirm whether Acme prefers quarterly invoicing for the first year (we recommend quarterly invoicing aligned to the quarterly true-up) or monthly invoicing with quarterly reconciliation?
3) Marissa/Pricing: finalize the pricing_grid_acme.xlsx numbers and provide the final discount ladder so we can embed numbers in the DocuSign envelope.

Attachments: final_terms_v2.pdf (PDF — terms with master schedule + opt-in auto-renew clause)
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2027-Q3
